extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism claims from XML/PDF text and constrained them to direct phenotype/pharmacology evidence plus an explicitly non-direct author hypothesis.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AcT-2 has direct smooth-muscle pharmacological activity in rat tail artery and urinary bladder preparations, with different response directions and potencies.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is pharmacological phenotype evidence, not a molecular receptor or antimicrobial mechanism assignment.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AcT-2 inhibits growth of model microorganisms in MIC assays; the local paper supports phenotypic antimicrobial activity but not a direct antimicrobial molecular target.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: synthetic AcT-2 against S. aureus, E. coli, and C. albicans
mechanism_claims.limitations: MIC evidence supports antimicrobial phenotype only; no membrane permeabilization, binding, or intracellular target assay is reported.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The discussion proposes that AcT-2 may be non-lytic or intracellular-targeted because it is short and shows low hemolysis; this remains an author hypothesis.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: mechanism interpretation for AcT-2 antimicrobial action
mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not classify as direct membrane disruption or intracellular target mechanism; local material lacks direct mechanism experiments.

caution_findings.note: No direct antimicrobial molecular mechanism assay is present locally; author speculation is preserved as indirect/hypothesis only.
